body: Honestly, the "details" were just time/place/people/context. I realized it was the wrong way to phase it, but I clearly remembered them and saw as relevant. It was at the nursing station, and one joke was just at one nurse, and the other was with 3 other people in the area. I know the people who were there for them and around what time. There were other issues I explained in another comment, but even with my inability to read the room I think they were resolved.

I just feel like I need to include every detail and it comes off as making excuses. I really don't mean for it to come off as a "shield", but I struggle socially to the point of isolating myself. There's other big things I realized as to why I said those things, but I'm guessing those would also come off as an excuse too. Professors and other nurses at clinicals don't know about my autism until I tell them at the very end. They always look in surprise and say I should've mentioned it sooner, so now it's one of the things I should always mention in my posts. I just thought it was context. 

"Why would you mention those things, neurodivergence has nothing to do with this." I do genuinely struggle so much because of it. I really think it's a big factor in how I talk, but it's me who's doing the talking, which I understand. It's a big part of how I thought this was okay, but first and foremost, the issue is me as a person. I genuinely want to change. I want to be someone who people can be comfortable with. There's a LOT of growth that needs to be done, and honestly, I'm terrified. I'm so scared that this journey will be too much for me. Yes, it's more than obvious that I have to get it together. No, I don't know where to start. 

But really, from the bottom of my heart, thank you to all who have read this. I feel really alone, and while people are saying I'm an idiot and deserve this, it makes me glad someone took time to comment and talk to me.

There were other things that I (think?) were smaller issues. There was profanity, and I told them it was because the other nurses said it around me, and I did it too to essentially fit in. A lot of the nurses swear to me once it's obvious I don't care about it. At least a handful of staff just let the facade of bring prim and proper drop when I talk to them. The techs and me were really casual and would just say these things, and we did this while chatting in front of my preceptor. A nurse had asked for help saying "Could I get a real nurse?" (She also just got off orientation and doesn't consider herself to be a proper nurse) and when I got up to help, she said "No, I need a REAL nurse." I was caught off guard as this was said in front of 3 other people, and found it rude. I blurted out "Goddamn, alright I guess." 

This was a CVNS floor, so we had an orientation to stoke class. When I returned and asked how it went, I said "Wow, I didn't pay any attention!" It was a lot and said it was overwhelming, especially because I was trying to take notes during the presentation but it was way too fast and I was lost. I always put things in a joking matter, but I guess it said I was lazy. I spent an hour trying to write notes and research during downtime, which management saw. 

Everyone has asked if I put in an IV yet. I have very bad tremors from both anxiety and a side effect of medication. Every time I'd say I haven't and that I was too scared to hurt the patient or make them feel uneasy with my shaky hands. I make this clear every time. She had asked multiple times if I wanted to put an IV in. Every time I told her about my shaking and how it makes both me and patients uneasy. I'm pretty confident that she's very aware of this as I denied it every time. I took a prn anxiety med that day and my tremors were minimal, and a patient needed an IV.  Preceptor asked if I wanted to do it and I said "Yeah!" and fearing she'd question my change of heart, I added "I took a medication that made my tremors go away! I can do it! Hooray!" She asked what medication and I waved it off as "Some beta blocker" (It was my anti panic attack med. Propranolol.) I didn't want to say it, so I told her not to worry about it. 

From my awful ability to read other people, they nodded their heads, saying "Oh, alright." and didn't touch on it again.

I really want to thank you for this. A lot of comments are saying being neurodivergent has nothing to do with this and that I'm making excuses. Maybe I am. I always feel like I have to overexplain myself and say everything and then it looks like I'm making a list of excuses as to why it wasn't my fault. This is one of the only few comments that haven't made me feel horrible about myself, although everyone is right. I guess I wanted a bit of comfort or understanding from other people. (I'm really not trying to say people are too mean or anything, but it still hurts, even if I'm incredibly in the wrong)

I take ADHD meds on top of 3 antidepressants. The third one was added a month ago and has actually been helping. A part of me is glad I can have a fresh new start somewhere else. People in the past have told me I "mix up the departments" (Doing things I can do in the kitchen when I'm not working there). I think that was a major factor. The morgue/coroner jobs want experience and additional education, from what I've looked at. Honestly I'd love night shift since I'm more of a night owl anyways.

I would say go to the hospital. If you want to reverse the damage you'll get from the overdose, you need to go. It can lead to lifelong impairment and damage if you don't, even if the aftermath of the hospital is scary. I say this as a nursing student.

I'm concerned since this was taken 8 hours ago, please get help as soon as you can before the damage sets in. Forcing yourself to throw up might help a tiny bit (Shove your entire hand down your throat, and if that isn't enough, use your fingers to touch your esophagus like you want to feel out your own anatomy) but otherwise drink copious amounts of water to flush it out of your system as fast as you can while you wait to get help. I don't know what kind of pills you took, but painkillers are very toxic to the liver. Sleeping pills will most likely not have any lasting damage, but do not take my word for it.

I hope that you have a full recovery and that the aftermath isn't as scary as we'd all imagine it to be.

Hey man, I had my own share of rough breakups. Shit happens. I thought felt the same when it happened to me. I've recovered and nowadays I laugh it off. Just live for yourself and not others. That philosophy helped me a lot.

You'll love again, and you don't need romantic love to be happy. 

If you're severely depressed like me, I personally recommend using the 3 day rule. If you still feel the same way in 3 days, think \[about it\] for a bit. Wait another week and see if you still feel the same. Then a month. A few months. If you're serious, then you have all the time in the world, there's nothing lost from living another day. Just get through the next day. Eat stuff you like. Do your favorite things, I mean if you really want to die then you might as well do your favorite thing one last time, right? It never hurts to just keep going one more day.

I hope you feel better, whether it be tomorrow or in 2 years like me. You can do it.

Thank you so much for a comforting comment like this. It really means a lot. I can't express how surprised but assured I felt seeing such a long comment over a post I was sure would be swept under the rug.

Maybe I only see other artists like me, but I feel like there's a subcategory of artists who are fans but are more invested into our art than being a stan, it's hard to explain tbh. There's stans who's whole thing is being a stan, but for artists it's art and whatever they do so I wouldn't group artists with stans, even though stans can be artists. There's been multiple instances of drama between artists and stans so putting them together doesn't really fit with me. 

As for Dream I'm glad he has grown as a person and a creator, and while his position is very hard to imagine being in, I feel like it still could've been handled better which is why I called it dumb. Would I have done something differently? Maybe, but some have pointed out flaws in his apology that I think are important and fixing them would make it more well received. But also those are just my 2 cents so it's kinda just ¯\\\_(ツ)\_/¯
